Page73 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version Figure 4.20: Utilities Area 4.5.9 SITE ROADWAYS Roads and access ways should facilitate easy movement for mobile equipment during construction, operation, maintenance, firefighting, and emergency evacuation. Additionally, roadways should be at least 3 meters away from processing equipment and road edges to provide a buffer against potential vehicle collisions. Typically, primary access roads to and from the site will be 6 meters wide, while secondary roads will be 4 meters wide. All these requirements have been met with the current site arrangement. Certain areas will require a larger turn radius to accommodate semi-trucks or 25 m³ CO 2 trucks (e.g., main access to the site, adjacent to train/truck offloading arms). Port Tampa Bay’s civil engineering subcontractor has performed a swept path analysis for appropriately sized tanker trucks which will be incorporated into the roadway design in the FEED stage. The plans and figures provided herein depict a few options for secondary roadways or evacuation paths out of the site in the event of an emergency. Some possibilities have been incorporated into the site Page74 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version layout, with the primary access located on the southwest side and the secondary access on the southeast side. Fig. 4.21 shows a plan view of the site highlighting the potential roadway access points and on-foot egress points. Future considerations for alternative road and foot access and egress points will be reviewed during subsequent project phases as the design and layout mature. Coordination with offsite utility providers and adjacent industrial site operators will become increasingly important during the FEED phase to optimize site road access points if necessary. The northeast corner of the site is a potential secondary road access point as it will tie into a north/south “future access road” on the east side of the site shown on existing PTB site plans. Figure 4.21: T-RICH Site Roads and Access Points 4.5.10 RAIL ACCESS The feasibility of delivering CO to the site via 100 cubic meter rail tanks has been assessed during this 2 Pre-FEED phase. An existing rail line south of the site can be used to provide rail access just west of the primary roadway. The site can accommodate twelve DOT class-105 pressure tank rail cars on two parallel tracks, accessible via three offloading arms for either rail tanks or trucks.
